clue.text: Tom's company in painful squeeze

parts.note: Tom Thumb, the tiny hero of the folk tale, gives the possessive form of his surname
a crew is a company of people working together, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A man named Tom and his firm are caught in an agonising financial squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' suggests an ordinary man, but it points to Tom Thumb of the nursery tale; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval torture device crushed the victim's digits, a literally agonising press.

clue.text: Model remains with this to face!

definitions.text: Model remains with this to face!

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so Model can stand for T
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A fashion model is told to add some facial hair to complete the look.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T is Ford's early car; ashes are the remains of something burnt. The whole clue also hints at hair worn on the upper lip.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word for a moustache, which is worn on the face.

clue.text: Atop one or two prepositions

definitions.meaning: on top of, a preposition of position
written solid it is one preposition; split into its two halves it is two

explanation.surface: A grammar point about whether one word or two words of position are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on top of, and split in the middle it yields two separate prepositions of direction and place.

clue.text: Cook thoroughly before biting flan

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
well means thoroughly, as in well done
tart means sharp or biting in taste

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: cook the pastry fully before getting your teeth into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting' looks like eating but means sharp-tasting; 'before' is a link. A Bakewell tart is an English almond and jam pastry named after a Derbyshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: This English almond-and-jam pastry is a type of open tart, so a kind of flan.

clue.text: I left broken biscuit for artist

indicators.note: something broken is shattered into pieces, so the remaining letters are rearranged
here left means departed, so the letter I goes away from the word

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a crumbled biscuit for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' tells you to drop the I from BISCUIT, leaving BSCUIT; 'broken' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Cubism, like Picasso or Braque, is a kind of painter.

clue.text: Former party member, with personal assistant, leaves French capital with bookplate

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of that political party

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so these letters are dropped from the city

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: An ex-politician and an aide quit Paris, taking a book label with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departure in the story, and it is: PA leaves PARIS, leaving RIS. 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'from the books of', a label pasted inside a volume naming its owner.

clue.text: Take over

parts.note: read as cricket: the player delivering the ball takes an over of six deliveries in turn

explanation.surface: Seize control of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls delivered by one player, so taking an over means delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this verb means to deliver the ball, and one player does so for a whole over.

clue.text: Failed to notice that it was supervised

definitions.meaning: missed or neglected to see something
was watched over by someone in charge

explanation.surface: Someone missed something that was being watched over all along.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means missed, and also, as a passive, watched over from above by a supervisor.

clue.text: Releasing Gilbertian medley

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A medley of Gilbert and Sullivan songs sets the audience free.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbertian means in the comic style of W. S. Gilbert of Gilbert and Sullivan operettas; 'medley' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting free is a synonym of freeing or emancipating.

clue.text: Baby-carrier found in the garden

parts.note: a bird said in folklore to bring babies has a beak, and a garden plant is named after that beak

explanation.surface: A pram or baby sling left out among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: Folklore says storks deliver babies; the plant is a wild geranium whose seed pods look like the bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild geranium (Erodium) named for its long beak-shaped fruit, grown or found in gardens.

clue.text: Auntie comes back unchanged

indicators.note: the word reads the same when taken from back to front, so it is unchanged when turned round

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An aunt returns from her trip just the same as before.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie and the Beeb are both British nicknames for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate British nicknames for the BBC, the national broadcaster.

clue.text: What he does on stage is moving but only at intervals

definitions.text: What he does on stage is moving but only at intervals

parts.words: What he does on stage is moving but only at intervals
parts.note: a theatre worker shifts the set, and only between acts or during scene changes

explanation.surface: A review of an actor whose performance is only occasionally touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to mean emotionally touching, but it is literal: shifting scenery. 'Intervals' are the breaks in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand who changes the scenery between scenes in a theatre.

clue.text: Dare-devil takes second to clean shield

parts.note: to wash is to clean
a buckler is a small round shield

explanation.surface: A risk-taker uses a moment to polish his shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link joining the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering, daring adventurer, like a pirate hero in films, is a reckless daredevil.

clue.text: Strands fellow worker in the field

parts.note: to strand a ship is to ground it, so strands gives grounds
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man leaves his colleague stuck out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strands' looks like a noun (threads) but is a verb: grounds, as of a ship run aground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after a sports pitch or park works on that field.

clue.text: Get on with support for group of people

parts.note: to get on is to grow old, to age
a bracket is a shelf support fixed to a wall

explanation.surface: Advice to get along with others and back a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of people classified together by how old they are, e.g. the over-sixties.

clue.text: Energy in Elgar composition at feast

indicators.note: in means the letter for energy goes inside the reworked name
a composition is something put together, so the composer's name letters are arranged anew

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An energetic Elgar piece is performed at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like a piece of music by Elgar, but it rearranges ELGAR; E goes inside that rearrangement. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain lavishly with food and drink, to treat guests to a banquet.

clue.text: It shows one the way to finish correspondence

parts.note: to sign is to finish a letter with a signature
post means letters, correspondence

explanation.surface: Advice on how to end a letter properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish correspondence' reads as one idea, ending a letter, but each word supplies its own piece; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer gives directions to travellers.

clue.text: Serviceman's order, duck

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is a serviceman

parts.note: a command is an order
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A soldier is ordered to duck down.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, so it gives O. 'Serviceman's' is 'serviceman is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier trained for raids is a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Open one's lip?

parts.note: the idiom button your lip means stay silent, so the opposite would be to open it up

explanation.surface: A question about speaking up after keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Button your lip' means keep quiet, so the clue's question turns that idiom around to mean speaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo fastenings, as on a coat; here applied to the idiom about keeping the mouth shut.

clue.text: Mainly behind

parts.note: the main is the open sea, so this is behind as said on the sea

explanation.surface: For the most part, running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the sea: this is behind in sailors' language.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for towards the back of a ship, behind it at sea.

clue.text: Warning about the way Tom included

indicators.note: included means the tom contains the road inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Ave is the abbreviation for Avenue, a way or street

explanation.surface: A caution regarding the route that Tom took.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a tomcat; 'about the' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal caution or proviso, from the Latin for 'let him beware'.

clue.text: Graphic figure has many a convulsion

parts.note: a diagram is a figure in a book
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a tic is an involuntary twitch or convulsion

explanation.surface: A drawing shows a figure having a severe fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; M stands for a thousand, a crossword way to say 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presented in the form of charts or drawings, a visual or pictorial representation.

clue.text: In the haze bumped into ox

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In the fog, someone collided with a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link joining the hidden letters to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A humped breed of cattle from South Asia, a kind of domesticated bovine.

clue.text: Long to take the item with honour

parts.note: it means the thing or item referred to
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Wanting to receive the object along with a knighthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn; CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a craving, as in being keen for something, a restless desire.

clue.text: All right in middle east to find donkey

indicators.note: in places the okay inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone checks the Middle East is fine to look for a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link. The answer is British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word for an ass or burro.

clue.text: Amount laid out in clothing

definitions.meaning: a sum of money put into something
an old sense: something one is clad in, from vest

explanation.surface: Money spent on a wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money put into a venture; also, in an old sense, garments one is dressed in.

clue.text: Sound comment

explanation.surface: A sensible remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tone is a sound, and a jotted remark is a comment.

clue.text: Made contact by phone having reached destination

definitions.meaning: a caller connected to the person they rang
arrived at the end of the journey

explanation.surface: A caller finally connected after arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone connection succeeded, and a traveller completed a passage to the end.
